title: Bank of England MPC decision + Monetary Policy Report (29 July 2027) — the first MPR published after the Jul-Sep 2027 cap takes effect, and the first to forecast off a fully post-VAT-reversion CPI path
source: EST: bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/upcoming-mpc-dates, fetched direct 2026-09-11 (HTTP 200) — the Bank's own published schedule lists 'Thursday 29 July' among its 2027 announcement dates and marks it as carrying a Monetary Policy Report. The page heads the year '2027 provisional dates' in the Bank's own words, so estimate is the Bank's label, not this lane's doubt; market-events-data.ts also defines no confirmed prefix for the Bank of England (the same standing taxonomy gap uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01 flagged across five non-US primaries). Discovered 2026-09-11 during the never-assessed initial research of ofgem-price-cap-announcement-2027-05-26
notes: PROPOSED BY THE ofgem-price-cap-announcement-2027-05-26 LANE, 2026-09-11, FROM THE BANK'S OWN 2027 SCHEDULE FETCHED BY THIS LANE. Why it is worth a slot rather than being left as the next routine MPC: the 2027 MPC dates already on this calendar stop being useful exactly where the UK electricity VAT reversion stops being forecastable. uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01 established the sequencing problem — the 2027-04-29 MPR must publish a forecast EMBEDDING the reversion having seen no post-reversion data, and 2027-06-17 (already proposed twice) is the first committee to SEE the April print. Neither is the first committee to publish a forecast built on observed post-reversion data: 2027-06-17 carries no Monetary Policy Report. 29 July 2027 is the first MPR after the observation, and it lands 28 days after the Jul-Sep 2027 cap takes effect on 1 July 2027, so it is also the first MPR whose near-term energy path is set by a cap this calendar tracks the announcement of. It is the natural scoring venue for whether the Bank looked through the notch, which uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01 predicted it would. Nothing in Jul/Aug/Sep 2027 on this calendar is UK: the quarter tracks only US and Japan events, so this is a genuine gap rather than a duplicate. Tiered LOW to match every other UK entry here: symbols [], no UK listing, gilt or sterling instrument in this calendar's eight-name US universe. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
